proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question asks for a smallest number of required evaluations without defining the admissible algorithm, the information returned by an evaluation, symbolic preprocessing, dominance pruning, or the cost measure. Ten realizable candidate incidences therefore do not imply a ten-query lower bound. The proposed wording narrows the question to a well-typed complexity claim within an explicitly specified model and leaves the mathematical issue open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: After an admissible evaluation/query model is specified, determine the exact worst-case evaluation cap by proving either a reduction below ten or a matching lower bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core defines the geometric candidate set but not an information or cost model. Distinct candidate incidences lower-bound the size of the unpruned set, not the number of objective queries required by every exact procedure, because algebraic dominance tests may eliminate candidates without querying their root values.
open_obligations.attempted: The boundary arrangement was reduced to at most five polygon vertices, four stationary-line contacts, and one informativeness-edge contact. An explicit strictly compatible configuration realizes all ten locations, but this does not distinguish direct enumeration from algorithms allowed symbolic pruning.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The ten-point closed-model envelope, constructive endpoint attainment, strict-model bound transfer and exact strict-attainment criterion, exact projection, and \(O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) width rate are proved above. The exact minimal universal evaluation cap remains open: ten is a proved complete candidate-map upper bound (eight when the informativeness cut is absent), not a proved minimum. Assay transport is maintained prospectively and is not inferred from trial blinding. Infinite odds endpoints, zero informativeness, covariate-dependent channels, and an empirical reanalysis of PolackEtAl2020 remain outside the formal claim.
